diagnosis: LOW_YIELD was partly a compact-frontier observability defect, not a shortage of executable recovery. The full allocator exposed seven recovery jobs requiring only unrestricted_public_http_origin_fetch, but the compact /wc frontier published zero HTTP-only candidates because browser-heavy rows occupied the bounded candidate/byte window. Therefore a runtime with real arbitrary public-origin HTTP but no representative JavaScript browser could appear idle despite compatible recovery.
intervention: Changed compact frontier ordering without changing allocator authority or job semantics. The frontier now preserves the allocator-preferred first four candidates, then promotes up to eight first exemplars of previously unseen exact required_capabilities signatures before ordinary truncation. Added a regression fixture with eight browser-only rows followed by three HTTP-only rows under a six-candidate budget, added EFF054 and ratchet checks, and verified Live publication. The post-patch compact frontier now includes portfolio-tts-generic-text-surface-public-origin-attest-rerun-v1 with the exact HTTP-only signature; EFF054 was promoted to RATCHETED with before/after evidence.
remaining_boundary: EFF052 remains STATIC_GUARDED_PENDING_RUNTIME until a worker whose tool contract definitively lacks arbitrary public-origin HTTP/DNS encounters an HTTP-only candidate in its retained compatible calculation and records the preclaim skip causally. EFF053 remains pending until Jose V11 G000010 ages beyond the liveness window and unchanged SOURCE_DEBT is observed only in recovery_attention.
strategy_note: FRONTIER_FIRST governed this owned rescue unit by prioritizing restoration of hidden claimable execution capacity in the compact frontier over additional diagnosis.
authority_boundary: No Current, Human Accepted, Served, Catalog, credential or product-byte authority changed.
